title: add downgrade guard + transactional migration support to upgrade/rollback tooling for private-installer
author: Aisha Patel
description: Add comprehensive downgrade-guard logic and transactional schema migration support to the private-installer upgrade/rollback tooling. Motivation: customers running Redwood Private in regulated environments reported risk during patch rollups where a failed migration left the cluster in a state that prevented safe rollback. This PR implements: 1) version-pinning metadata written to the cluster at upgrade-start so automated rollbacks can detect incompatible version states; 2) a downgrade-guard check that prevents automatic downgrade when schema or data migrations would be lossy; 3) a transactional migration runner for Postgres (wrapper around pg_dump/checkpoint/tx) that ensures migrations are applied atomically and can be rolled back cleanly; 4) backup and restore hooks integrated with the existing installer's backup plan (S3/GCS support); 5) Helm chart annotations and a Terraform variable to surface upgrade strategy and require explicit opt-in for non-transactional migrations. The description below covers design, rollout plan, testing, and rollback semantics. Design summary: - Version pinning: installer writes a cluster annotation redwood.io/installed-version and redwood.io/migration-hash before applying any DB migration. The upgrade tool records both desired_version and migration_hints to object metadata and verifies compatibility with the target chart. - Downgrade guard: when attempting to downgrade, the tool compares current metadata with target metadata and will refuse automated downgrade if hashes differ or if migration_hints indicate incompatible irreversible changes; a --force-downgrade flag is available but requires an explicit human confirmation and an audit log entry. - Transactional migrations: adds a migration runner that wraps schema changes in a single transaction where possible; for operations that cannot be transactional (e.g., CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, certain VACUUM or ALTER TABLE operations), the runner will split work and record a two-phase marker to allow controlled rollback. - Backup/restore hooks: pre-upgrade step triggers a snapshot/export using the cluster's configured backup provider; if export fails the upgrade aborts. The restore path is wired to the rollback command to allow automated restoration on rollback or manual invocation. - Helm/Terraform: Chart values added: upgrade.transactionalMigrations (bool), upgrade.backupProvider (string), upgrade.versionPinning (bool). Terraform module adds variable require_explicit_downgrade (bool) that defaults to true for installs that require drift-safe upgrades. Rollout plan: start with canary customers on dedicated/private installs; enable feature-flagged behavior for first two weeks; collect telemetry via the console (upgrade_attempt, upgrade_success, backup_status). Testing: Unit tests for migration runner, e2e test harness that runs a real Postgres in CI using ephemeral K8s cluster (kind) and runs an upgrade/downgrade cycle with simulated failure modes. Manual QA with a staging private-installer build. Backwards compatibility: existing clusters without version-pinning metadata will be treated as pre-guarded and the tooling will require a one-time acceptance to adopt version pinning. Related Linear: ENG-4321, ENG-4408. Related PRs: referenced earlier private-installer backup/restore PRs and schema migration cleanup. Security: audit events are emitted for forced downgrades and backup exports. Ops guidance: added a section to the private-installer README and console runbook describing how to recover from forced-downgrade scenarios.
commits: 4 commits: 1) add transactional migration runner and unit tests; 2) add version pinning metadata + checks; 3) backup/restore hooks + CI job to exercise backup provider; 4) helm and terraform variable additions + docs updates
review_comments: Jonah Kim: Left a few nits around error messages and suggested making the --force-downgrade flow emit a console confirmation prompt (addressed in commit 3).
Priya Desai: Asked for explicit telemetry events for backup success/failure and suggested adding an Alerting doc to SLOs/alerts (added docs).
Marco Silva: Requested a clearer failure invariant for non-transactional migrations; updated runner to write two-phase markers and added tests.

release_notes: Added downgrade-guard and transactional migration support to private-installer upgrade tooling; default behavior backs up cluster before upgrade and pins version metadata to prevent unsafe downgrades. Requires operators to opt-in to non-transactional migrations.
